intervention_dose: oral niraparib 200-300 mg once daily, individualized starting dose by body weight and baseline platelet count
indication: newly diagnosed advanced high-grade serous/endometrioid ovarian cancer, response after 1L platinum
population_detail: All-comers, both HRD-positive and HRD-negative strata; no BRCA mutation and no validated HRD score required for enrolment. The all-comer enrolment is what makes PRIMA the cleanest fit for this BRCA-proficient, genomically-unstable tumor.
median_dor_or_pfs: mPFS 13.8 mo niraparib vs 8.2 mo placebo (overall)

outcomes.name: HR_OS
outcomes.notes: OS rate 84% vs 77%; immature at primary report

safety_summary: Hematologic toxicity dominated. Grade 3+ anemia 31%, thrombocytopenia 28.7%, neutropenia 12.8%. Individualized starting dose reduced grade 3+ thrombocytopenia versus the fixed-dose cohort.

toxicities.notes: dose-limiting; flagged against patient's myelosuppression veto

notes: Pivotal 1L all-comer maintenance trial behind niraparib's broad label. The BRCA-WT, genomically-unstable profile here qualifies via the all-comer rationale rather than any BRCA gate; HRD-positive subgroup shows larger benefit but enrolment never required it. Triggers the patient's severe-myelosuppression toxicity veto, partly mitigated by individualized starting dose.

intervention_dose: oral rucaparib 600 mg twice daily, up to 24 months
indication: newly diagnosed advanced high-grade epithelial ovarian cancer, response after 1L platinum doublet
population_detail: All-comers (4:1 randomization), HRD-positive and HRD-negative strata. Benefit held in the ITT population and in the non-nested HRD-negative subgroup, so a BRCA-WT, HRD-unquantified tumor still qualifies.
design: randomized double-blind placebo-controlled phase 3, 1L maintenance (ATHENA-MONO / GOG-3020 / ENGOT-ov45)
median_dor_or_pfs: mPFS 20.2 mo rucaparib vs 9.2 mo placebo (ITT)
safety_summary: Grade 3+ anemia 28.7%, neutropenia 14.6%, transaminase elevation 10.6%. AE-related discontinuation 11.8%. Transaminase rises were usually transient and the patient's baseline LFTs are normal.

toxicities.notes: usually transient; baseline LFTs normal in this patient

notes: Second all-comer 1L PARP-maintenance option. ITT HR 0.52 (95% CI 0.40-0.68) from the primary JCO publication (pmid 35658487). Qualifies the BRCA-WT tumor via the ITT/HRD-negative benefit, not a BRCA gate. Severe-myelosuppression veto applies.

intervention_dose: oral olaparib 300 mg twice daily for up to 24 months + bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV q3w to 15 months total
indication: newly diagnosed advanced high-grade serous ovarian cancer receiving 1L bevacizumab
population_detail: All-comers enrolled, but the predefined and label-relevant benefit is in the HRD-positive subgroup (Myriad MyChoice GIS >=42 or tumor BRCA mutation). This patient is BRCA wild-type and has only a qualitative Altera instability call, so eligibility is CONTINGENT on a validated GIS she does not yet have.
design: randomized double-blind placebo-controlled phase 3, olaparib vs placebo added to bevacizumab backbone (PAOLA-1 / ENGOT-ov25)

outcomes.name: HR_PFS
outcomes.notes: mPFS 37.2 vs 17.7 mo; the label-relevant estimand

outcomes.name: HR_PFS
outcomes.notes: mPFS 28.1 vs 16.6 mo; closest analogue to this BRCA-WT patient IF a validated GIS confirms HRD-positive

safety_summary: Grade 3+ AE ~57% in the combination arm. Grade 3+ hypertension 19%, anemia 17%, lymphopenia 7%, fatigue/asthenia 5%. Up to 20% discontinued olaparib for AEs. Bevacizumab-driven hypertension and VTE/bleeding risk are relevant given this patient's VTE history and prior IVC filter.

toxicities.notes: bevacizumab class effect; relevant to VTE/bleeding caution

notes: Highest-magnitude PARP option (HRD-positive HR 0.33) and the patient is already on the bevacizumab backbone, but it is contingent: PAOLA-1 benefit concentrates in HRD-positive disease defined by MyChoice GIS >=42 or tumor BRCA. Altera's qualitative instability call does not meet that companion-diagnostic threshold. The BRCA-non-mutated HRD-positive subgroup (HR 0.43) is the relevant comparator only if a validated GIS comes back >=42; below that she is HRD-negative and defaults to all-comer niraparib. Combination-arm grade 3+ AE per PMC10859514 expert review.

intervention_dose: bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV q3w with chemotherapy then maintenance to ~15 months total
indication: newly diagnosed stage III-IV epithelial ovarian / primary peritoneal cancer
population_detail: All-comers, no biomarker selection. Matches the VEGF/angiogenesis axis the patient is already being treated on.
median_dor_or_pfs: mPFS 14.1 mo bev-throughout vs 10.3 mo control

outcomes.name: HR_PFS
outcomes.notes: mPFS 14.1 vs 10.3 mo; OS not significantly improved

safety_summary: Hypertension requiring therapy 22.9% in the bevacizumab-throughout arm vs 7.2% control. GI-wall disruption 2.6% vs 1.2%. No neuropathy or myelosuppression veto triggered by bevacizumab itself; the relevant caution is VTE/bleeding given this patient's VTE history and prior IVC filter.

toxicities.notes: requiring medical therapy; bev-throughout arm vs 7.2% control

notes: Anchors the bevacizumab maintenance axis the patient is already on. PFS benefit only; OS was not improved in the overall population. VTE/bleeding caution is the operative concern here, not the patient's named neuropathy or myelosuppression vetoes.

intervention_dose: bevacizumab 7.5 mg/kg IV q3w with chemotherapy then maintenance to ~12 months
indication: newly diagnosed epithelial ovarian / primary peritoneal cancer
population_detail: All-comers, no biomarker gate. OS benefit concentrated in the high-risk subset (stage IV or suboptimally debulked); this stage IIIc R0 patient sits adjacent to that subset.
median_dor_or_pfs: mPFS 21.8 mo bev vs 20.3 mo control (36-mo cut)

outcomes.name: OS
outcomes.notes: vs 28.8 mo control; OS benefit limited to high-risk subgroup

safety_summary: Bevacizumab added more toxicity, most often grade 2+ hypertension (18% vs 2% with chemotherapy alone). VTE/bleeding caution applies given the patient's VTE history; no neuropathy or myelosuppression veto triggered.
notes: Reinforces the bevacizumab axis; largest benefit in the high-risk subgroup. Open-label design so RoB is some-concern. OS gain limited to the high-risk subset.

indication: ER-positive high-grade serous ovarian cancer, maintenance / later-line
population_detail: ER-positive HGSOC by IHC; a translational study with a clinical letrozole-maintenance series, enriched for platinum-resistant and residual-disease patients. The patient is ER-positive (~80% nuclei) but PR-negative, which tempers expected magnitude.
design: translational study with retrospective clinical letrozole-maintenance comparison (TCGA/IHC analysis + treated cohort)
median_dor_or_pfs: RFS benefit favoring letrozole; control mRFS ~13.2 mo
safety_summary: No per-term toxicity table in the source; aromatase-inhibitor class toxicity is arthralgia and bone-density loss on prolonged use. Oral, low-burden, no named patient veto applies.
notes: Low-toxicity oral option that fits the patient's age and oral-preference, but the evidence is a non-randomized retrospective comparison nested in a translational ESR1/ER-expression study, not the single-arm phase 2 the trials.jsonl row described - flag the design mismatch. Benefit modest and tempered by PR-negativity. No per-term AE table in source (translational paper, no safety section); toxicities left empty accordingly.

intervention_dose: intraperitoneal IMNN-001 (GEN-1) 100 mg/m2 weekly with neoadjuvant/adjuvant carboplatin-paclitaxel
indication: newly diagnosed advanced epithelial ovarian cancer, neoadjuvant + interval debulking
population_detail: Advanced epithelial ovarian cancer treated with neoadjuvant chemotherapy plus IP IL-12 immunogene. Regimen-matched to this patient, who received GEN-1 with neoadjuvant carbo/paclitaxel and achieved R0. Acts via the tumor immune microenvironment, so the foreclosed MSS/TMB-low checkpoint axis does not exclude it.
design: randomized phase 1/2 added to neoadjuvant chemotherapy (OVATION 2 / NCT03393884)
median_dor_or_pfs: mPFS 14.9 mo IMNN-001 vs 11.9 mo control (ITT)

outcomes.name: HR_PFS
outcomes.notes: mPFS 14.9 vs 11.9 mo; sponsor topline / Gynecol Oncol 2025

outcomes.name: HR_OS
outcomes.notes: ~13-mo median OS improvement; immature, longer follow-up

safety_summary: Sponsor and abstract report IP delivery generally well tolerated with no new safety signal; no per-term grade 3+ AE table in the public topline / abstract. No named patient toxicity veto implicated.
notes: Regimen-matched investigational program the patient is already on. Efficacy from sponsor topline (Imunon, Oct 2024) and the Gynecol Oncol 2025 abstract; the full peer-reviewed paper (publisher page 403) and ClinicalTrials.gov AE tab were not accessible, so no per-term toxicities extracted - backfill when full text opens. CI bounds not reported in the topline. FDA has cleared a phase 3 program.

indication: advanced solid tumors with PIK3CA alterations (biomarker-selected basket)
population_detail: Biomarker-matched baskets keyed on PIK3CA mutation OR amplification. The patient has focal somatic PIK3CA amplification; benefit data for amplification (as opposed to activating hotspot mutation) are weak, and there is no approved PI3K-directed therapy in ovarian cancer.
outcome: objective response rate / safety (no mature efficacy for PIK3CA-amplified ovarian cancer)

outcomes.name: biomarker
outcomes.notes: PIK3CA amplification is a trial-matching tag; no validated efficacy estimand in this setting

safety_summary: PI3Kalpha-pathway class toxicity is hyperglycemia, rash, diarrhea, and stomatitis; no published per-term rates for the specific PIK3CA-amplified ovarian-cancer context. No named patient veto directly implicated.
notes: Context-only row kept clearly investigational. There is no approved PI3K/AKT therapy in HGSOC and amplification is a poorly-validated predictive marker versus activating mutation. Surfaced so the board sees the PI3K axis the Altera report flagged; not a ranked option. No primary-source efficacy or AE data to extract (early-phase baskets without ovarian-specific readouts).

intervention_dose: trastuzumab deruxtecan 5.4 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks
indication: previously treated HER2-expressing advanced ovarian cancer (DESTINY-PanTumor02 ovarian cohort)
population_detail: Ovarian cohort enrolled at HER2 IHC 2+ or 3+. This patient is IHC 1+, below that entry bar, so the ovarian activity reported here comes from a higher-expression population than hers.
design: open-label single-arm phase 2 pan-tumor basket, ovarian cohort
median_dor_or_pfs: mDoR 11.3 mo (95% CI 4.1-22.1); mPFS 5.9 mo; mOS 13.2 mo (ovarian cohort)

outcomes.name: ORR
outcomes.notes: n=75; activity concentrates at the 3+ tier

safety_summary: Grade 3+ treatment-related AEs in 40.8% across the seven cohorts. Adjudicated drug-related ILD/pneumonitis hit 10.5%, with three fatal cases, so lung monitoring is the defining risk.
notes: Closest tumor-type evidence: the ovarian cohort responded at 45%, but it enrolled IHC 2+/3+ and the tumor-agnostic T-DXd approval needs IHC 3+. For this IHC 1+ tumor the drug is off-label, so the row sits as activity-ceiling context rather than a matched option.

intervention_dose: trastuzumab deruxtecan 5.4 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks
indication: previously treated HER2-low (IHC 1+ or 2+/ISH-) metastatic breast cancer
population_detail: HER2-low breast cancer; the hormone-receptor-positive subgroup mirrors this patient's ER-positive status. Direct evidence that an IHC 1+ tumor responds to T-DXd, though the disease is breast rather than ovarian.
design: randomized open-label phase 3 (2:1) vs physician's choice chemotherapy
median_dor_or_pfs: mPFS 10.1 vs 5.4 mo (HR+); mOS 23.9 vs 17.5 mo (HR+)
safety_summary: Grade 3+ AEs in 52.6% on T-DXd vs 67.4% on chemotherapy. Adjudicated drug-related ILD/pneumonitis reached 12.1%, including 0.8% grade 5; nausea was near-universal.
notes: The off-label-precedent anchor for treating an IHC 1+ tumor with T-DXd, and the HR+ subgroup matches her ER-positive biology. It is breast, so she cannot enrol; efficacy from the NEJM abstract, per-term AE counts from the ClinicalTrials.gov AE tab (NCT03734029).

intervention_dose: trastuzumab deruxtecan 5.4 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks
indication: HR-positive HER2-low or HER2-ultralow metastatic breast cancer after endocrine therapy
population_detail: HR-positive disease spanning HER2-low and HER2-ultralow (IHC 0 with faint membrane staining). The ultralow stratum is the closest expression analog to her IHC 1+, ER-positive tumor.
design: randomized open-label phase 3 vs physician's choice chemotherapy

outcomes.name: HR_PFS
outcomes.notes: exploratory; consistent with HER2-low, not separately powered

safety_summary: Grade 3+ AEs in 52.8% on T-DXd vs 44.4% on chemotherapy. Adjudicated ILD/pneumonitis affected 49 patients (11.3%), with three grade 5 events.
notes: Pushes the HER2-low signal down to ultralow IHC 0 in HR-positive disease, the band her IHC 1+ tumor sits in. Published HER2-low PFS HR is 0.62 (0.52-0.75); the screener row listed 0.64, so flag that for reconciliation. Per-term GI/heme AE not in the abstract; ILD and the union grade 3+ rate captured.

intervention_dose: trastuzumab deruxtecan 5.4 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks
indication: metastatic breast cancer across the HER2 expression range
population_detail: Three cohorts by HER2 tier: overexpressing (cohort 1), HER2-low IHC 1+/2+ISH- (cohort 2), and IHC 0 non-expressing (cohort 3). The IHC 0 cohort is the key read: responses held at the very bottom of HER2 expression, where her tumor sits.
design: open-label single-arm phase 2, three HER2-defined cohorts
safety_summary: Most common grade 3+ events were neutropenia 12%, fatigue 8%, and vomiting 6%. ILD/pneumonitis occurred in nine patients (5%), all grade 1-2; three grade 5 AEs overall.
notes: Shows T-DXd activity does not switch off at low or absent HER2, which is the mechanistic basis for treating her IHC 1+ tumor. Breast, not ovarian, and single-arm, so it informs rather than ranks.

intervention_dose: disitamab vedotin 2.0 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks
indication: HER2-positive (IHC 2+/3+) locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma
population_detail: HER2-positive urothelial carcinoma pooled from two phase 2 trials. Different tumor type and a higher HER2 tier than hers, but the best-powered published read on the drug's MMAE toxicity, which is what her neuropathy veto turns on.
design: combined analysis of two single-arm phase 2 trials (RC48-C005, RC48-C009)
median_dor_or_pfs: mDoR 7.3 mo; mPFS 5.9 mo; mOS 14.2 mo
safety_summary: Grade 3+ treatment-related AEs in 54.2%. Peripheral sensory neuropathy hit 68.2% any grade and 18.7% grade 3+, the MMAE signal that collides with her neuropathy veto; neutropenia 42.1% any, 12.1% grade 3+.

toxicities.notes: MMAE class effect; triggers patient neuropathy veto

notes: Kept mainly for the MMAE safety read: the 68% peripheral neuropathy and 12% grade 3+ neutropenia map straight onto her two named vetoes. HER2-positive urothelial, not ovarian HER2-low, so efficacy is mechanism context.

intervention_dose: disitamab vedotin 2.0 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks
indication: HER2-expressing metastatic breast cancer with PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway activation (HER2-low subgroup)
population_detail: Pretreated HER2-expressing breast cancer selected for PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway activation; 36 of 62 were HER2-low. The HER2-low response rate is the only published disitamab vedotin efficacy read in the low-expression tier, but the pathway selection and breast setting limit how far it carries to her ovarian tumor.
safety_summary: No per-term safety data in the available abstract text. MMAE-payload class effects are peripheral neuropathy and neutropenia, both named vetoes for this patient.
notes: The only published disitamab vedotin HER2-low efficacy datapoint (ORR ~34%), but PAM-pathway-selected breast cancer and abstract-only. Per-term AE not extractable: publisher page 403, no PMC ID, no ClinicalTrials.gov results record found, so toxicities left empty.

exclusion_reason: Program shelved after the FDA complete response letter on the HER2-positive breast filing and Byondis halted development; the phase 1 enrolled no ovarian patients.
notes: Phase 1 documented HER2-low (IHC 1+) breast activity and a duocarmazine ocular and pneumonitis profile distinct from the MMAE conjugates. Kept as mechanism context only, not a live option.
